---
title: "Multilingual sites"
---


The theme's answer to "the same site in two languages" is deliberately
boring: **one Quarto website project per language**, `en/` and `de/`,
rendered into `site/en/` and `site/de/`. No i18n framework, no
per-page front-matter pairing — just two projects whose sidebars list
the same pages in the same order.

That parallelism is not a convention to remember; it is checked. This
site is built exactly this way, as are qdaPy's and qdaR's.

## The language menu

Each project's navbar carries the translate icon with one entry per
language:

```yaml
- icon: translate
  aria-label: Language
  menu:
    - text: English
      href: ../en/index.html
    - text: Deutsch
      href: ../de/index.html
```

Out of the box those entries point at the other language's front page.
The generated map below retargets them to **the translation of the
page being read**.

## gen_langmap.py

`script/gen_langmap.py` takes the language directories as arguments
(`gen_langmap.py en de`), walks their sidebars in parallel and writes
the page-to-page map plus the retargeting logic as
`theme/scripts.html` into every project, which inlines it into every
page (`include-after-body` is depth-blind, so a relative
`<script src>` would only work from the site root — inlining sidesteps
that). The map carries all translations per page, so a third language
is one more argument, one more project directory and one more menu
entry — nothing in the script changes. `--extra-js` inlines further
scripts after the map; this documentation passes its version banner
(`shared/versions.js`) that way.

Deriving the map from the sidebars means it cannot fall behind a page
that was added. The cost is the rule the check enforces: **add a page
to every sidebar or to none** — if the sidebars stop being
parallel, the build fails with a message saying so, not a switcher
that silently sends readers to the wrong page.

The map's keys are site-root-relative (`en/guide/offline.html` ↔
`de/guide/offline.html`), so the same file works over http and from a
plain file tree.

## The language chooser at the root

Above the two language directories sits a small `index.html` that
forwards visitors to their browser language and shows two plain links
when JavaScript is off — which is also where the legal pages stay
reachable. `doc-root/index.html` in this repository is the copy this
site deploys; take it as a template.
